rationale: Both independently surface the exact latent gap (hunyuan_image3_transformer.py:2238 still calling the removed get_cache_scale API), with specific reachability chains through the pipeline/AutoWeightsLoader, so gap_hit is true for both. But Y goes further on the one substantive concern the human reviewer actually raised — that the tests use fakes and don't prove real-checkpoint/mapper fidelity — hitting it from five angles (CI not wired up, hardcoded allowlist, misleading test name, hand-rolled mapper diverging from the real WeightsMapper API, unrealistic MiMo naming) plus verifying the safe-removal claims against actual vLLM source (default_weight_loader, maybe_remap_kv_scale_name) and reporting an actual local test run. X's review is comparably well-grounded on the gap finding but padded with two near-duplicate 'general' findings about the same AR double-mapper nit, and covers the test-realism theme with only one finding versus Y's five, giving it materially lower recall against the ground-truth review's core critique. Both are concrete and file/line-anchored, but Y's clearer verdict-first structure and explicit fix snippets edge out X's denser, more redundant format on actionability.
